judgments.reason: The span 'A 31-year-old woman presented with a 7-year history of episodic palpitations, profuse sweating, and severe headaches.' appears literally in the vignette and clinically supports pheochromocytoma as a component of the completed diagnosis, since these are classic catecholamine-excess symptoms.

The span 'Over the same period, she noted a gradually enlarging anterior neck swelling without compressive symptoms or signs of thyroid dysfunction.' appears literally in the vignette and clinically supports medullary thyroid carcinoma as a component, as an enlarging thyroid mass is a key feature of MTC in MEN2.

The span '24-hour urinary metanephrines >10 000 µg (normal 25–312 µg) and normetanephrines 8791 µg (normal <600 µg)' appears literally in the vignette and directly supports pheochromocytoma as a component of the completed diagnosis through markedly elevated catecholamine metabolites.

The span 'Serum calcitonin 10 506 pg/mL (normal <11.5 pg/mL)' appears literally in the vignette and directly supports medullary thyroid carcinoma as a component, since massively elevated calcitonin is the biochemical hallmark of MTC.
